paper_title: Projected sensitivities of the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment to new physics via low-energy electron recoils
suggested_experiment_name: LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) electron recoil sensitivity to solar axions
coupling_convention: g_ae (dimensionless axion-electron coupling), canonical form as plotted on y-axis
notes: This paper presents PROJECTED SENSITIVITIES (not measured limits) for the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment to multiple new physics signals via low-energy electron recoils. The paper discusses 7 different signal types: (1) neutrino magnetic moment, (2) neutrino millicharge, (3) solar axions, (4) axion-like particles (ALPs), (5) hidden photons, (6) mirror dark matter, and (7) leptophilic dark matter. While the abstract mentions axion-electron coupling as a hint, the paper actually constrains MULTIPLE coupling types simultaneously across different signal models. The coupling types involved include: AxionElectron (solar axions via g_Ae, ALPs via g_Ae), DarkPhoton (hidden photons via kinetic mixing κ), and others. Because this is a multi-signal projection paper with no single dominant coupling type, and because the results are projections rather than measured exclusion limits, extraction of specific numerical data points is not appropriate. The paper presents sensitivity curves in Figures 4a-4f but these are PROJECTED sensitivities at 90% CL and 3σ evidence levels, not observed limits.
